(By Sri.K.M.Sanath Kumar/Ramagiriyamma,Adv)
 :JUDGMENT:
This is a Claim Petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident.

Saraswathi R vs B.M.T.C on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188720955/
1 2.

The Petition averments are as under:
That on 04.11.2023 at about 5.30 P.M., at Kalasipalya Bus Stop, the petitioner was waiting for the Bus to go home, when a BMTC Bus bearing no.KA-01-F-8934 came and halted; while the passengers started to board the bus, the petitioner also climbed the foot-rest of the bus, when the driver of the bus all of a sudden without waiting for the signal of conductor, moved the bus, as a result of which, the petitioner lost her balance and fell down from the bus and left rear- wheel of the bus ran over her left-leg.
As a result, the Petitioner fell-down and sustained Degloving-injury to her left-leg from knee to tip of the foot.
3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Victoria Hospital, where she was treated as an inpatient.

The petitioner spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards Medical treatment,
Conveyance, Nourishment Expenses and Attendant charges.
4. That prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale & healthy and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month from tailoring business but the accident led to permanent-disablement.
5. The Respondent being the Owner cum Insurer of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg.no.KA-01-F-8934 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence this Petition.
6. In pursuance of notice, the Respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the objections to main petition.
7. In the Objection Statement, the Respondent-BMTC has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also that the accident was due the rash and negligent driving of the BMTC Bus Driver.
It is contended that the driver of the bus was not at all responsible for the accident and the petitioner is solely responsible for the accident.
On these grounds, the Respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

8. On the rival pleadings, the following issues have been framed:
ISSUES

1. Whether the Petitioner proves that she has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01-F-8934 by its driver, in RTA took place on 04.11.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. on Kalasipalya Main Road, opp.Annapurna Hotel, BMTC stand, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
Saraswathi R vs B.M.T.C on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188720955/
2 9.

sentences.text: In support of her case, the petitioner has got herself examined as PW.1 and Exs.P.1 to 10 have been marked; a doctor has been examined as PW.2 and Exs.P.11 & 12 have been marked.

On the other hand, the Respondent has examined its Conductor as RW.1.
10.
Perused the pleadings and materials on record.
Heard both-sides.

My answer to these Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :

As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:-It is the case of Petitioner that she has sustained grievous-injuries in the accident caused by the driver of the offending BMTC Bus bearing no.KA-01-F-8934.
On the other hand, the Respondent has denied that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending BMTC bus.
12. In support of her case, the petitioner has got herself examined as PW.1 and Exs.P.1 to 10 have been marked; a Doctor has been examined as PW.2 and Exs.P.11 & 12 have been marked.

Exs.P.1 to 6 are the true-copy of FIR with Complaint, Statement, Crime detail form with sketch, IMV Report,
Wound Certificate and Charge sheet.

13. A perusal of FIR & Complaint at Exs.P.1 & 2 show that, City Market Traffic Police have filed the FIR against the driver of the offending BMTC bus bearing no.KA-01-F-8934 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC, on the complaint lodged by one Ashwini-Daughter of petitioner.
From the FIR & Complaint at Ex.P.1, it is also evident that the alleged accident has taken place on 04.11.2023 and the complaint has been lodged immediately on the next day.

As per the Complaint, on 04.11.2023 at about 5.30 P.M., at Kalasipalya Bus Stop, the complainant and her mother (petitioner) were waiting for the Bus to go home, when a BMTC Bus bearing no.KA-01-F-8934 came and halted; while the complainant boarded the bus and occupied the seat,
her mother/petitioner was about to board the bus along with other passengers, and in the meantime, the driver of the bus all of a sudden negligently moved the bus, due to which the petitioner lost her balance and fell-down from the bus, and the left rear-wheel of the bus ran over her left-leg; suddenly the public shouted and pulled the petitioner from the wheel.
Ex.P.2 is the Statement of Petitioner which is on same-lines as that of the complaint.
Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar and Sketch which describes and show the accident spot.
As per the IMV Report at Ex.P.4, no damages to the bus have been noticed.
There can be no documentary evidence as to who was negligent - the Petitioner or the Bus Driver, since 'negligence' is purely a factual aspect in this case.

[
14. However, the respondent-BMTC has examined its Conductor as RW.1 who has deposed as Saraswathi R vs B.M.T.C on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188720955/
3 under, in his examination- in-chief:
"That the driver has moved the bus slowly, cautiously by observing the traffic rules, at that time the petitioner all of a sudden tried to board the moving bus and fell- down and caused the accident."
Negligence apart, the above evidence of RW.1 corroborates the occurrence of accident, and also the fact that he was the Conductor of the offending bus at the time of accident.

15. No doubt, the respondent has denied the negligence of the offending bus driver, but the I.O. after thorough investigation, on the basis of the evidence of eye-witnesses, has filed the Charge- sheet at Ex.P.6 against the driver of the offending BMTC Bus and the said charge sheet remains unchallenged by its driver.

As already discussed above, the evidence of RW.1 coupled with the charge sheet is sufficient to hold that the accident is due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending BMTC Bus, in which the petitioner has sustained grievous-injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative".
16.
Issue No.2:-
Having proved that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. PW.1 has deposed that due to the accident, she has sustained injury to left-leg from knee to tip of the foot.

As per the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.5, the petitioner has sustained:
i) Swelling left left leg (ii) Tenderness over left leg and (iii) Degloving injuries to left leg.
As per the Discharge Summary at Ex.P.7, the petitioner has been treated as an inpatient from 04.11.2023 to 04.12.2023 and has undergone Wound Debridement VAC application and Skin Grafting.

18. The petitioner has examined Dr.Chidanand, Orthopaedic Surgeon, Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics, Bengaluru, as P.W.2 who has deposed that the petitioner has sustained Degloving injury to her left-leg and she has undergone Wound Debridement VAC application and Skin Grafting.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: But it is relevant to note that as per the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.5, there is no reference as to 'skin grafting', as deposed by PW.2 in his examination-in-chief.

In the absence of such reference, PW.2 who has admittedly not treated the petitioner and has deposed regarding the injury/treatment/disability of petitioner on the basis of documents viz., 'Wound Certificate',
'Discharge Summary', etc., could not have deposed about 'skin grafting'.
19. Further, PW.2 has produced the Clinical notes and X-ray at Exs.P.11 & 12, and has assessed the permanent physical disability to the whole body from lower limb at 12%.
But when from the documents on record it is clear that the petitioner has not suffered any injury to the bone, the question of considering the 'whole body' disability at 12% does not arise.
This also renders the X- Ray at Ex.P.12, doubtful.

The learned counsel for Respondent has thus cross-examined PW.2 on these lines, the relevant portion of which is as under:
Saraswathi R vs B.M.T.C on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188720955/
4

entities.text: Saraswathi R vs B.M.T.C on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have not treated the patient at any point of time.
While assessing the disabilities I have gone through the discharge summary and wound certificate.
No bone injuries are mentioned in the wound certificate and discharge summary.
It is true to suggest that the patient has been treated with wound debridement and skin grafting.
It is true to suggest that the patient has been treated by plastic surgery department.
2. I am an Orthopedic surgeon.
It is false to suggest that so far as the petitioner is concerned, plastic surgeon is the better person and expert to analyze the extent of disability of petitioner.
It is true to suggest that all the injuries of the petitioner have healed, the witness volunteers that the injuries have healed with secondary intention.
3. It is true to suggest that I have mentioned about the scars and there is no disability from those scars.
4. It is true to suggest that there are no documents to show that the petitioner has sustained bone injuries due to the accident.

20. From the Medical documents on record and evidence of PW.2, it is clear that the petitioner has not suffered any injury to any bone, but has only suffered the 'Degloving injury', as could be seen from the photographs at Exs.P10.
And for the said 'Degloving injury', the petitioner has undergone Wound Debridement VAC application only.

Thus in the absence of any physical or functional disability, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the Head 'Future loss of income'.
21.

However, having regard to the nature of injury sustained, the petitioner has undergone Pain,
Shock & Suffering.
She is thus entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'Pain, Shock and Suffering'.

Further, as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar - (2011) 1 SCC 343, adequate compensation ought to be awarded not only for the physical injury and treatment, but also for the loss of earning and her inability to lead a normal life and enjoy amenities, which she would have enjoyed but for the disability caused due to the accident.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar - (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus the petitioner who has to live with the 'scars' of the injury for the rest of her life is entitled for a sum of Rs. 50,000/- under the Head 'Loss of Amenities'.
22.
The Petitioner/PW.1 has deposed that she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
She has produced 48 medical bills at Ex.P.8 amounting Rs.82,003/- I have gone through the medical bills.
There is no serious dispute regarding the medical bills.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.82,003/- as compensation under the Head Medical Expenses.

23. Considering the above aspects, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation as under :
1. Pain & Suffering Rs. 1,00,000/-
2. Loss of Amenities Rs. 50,000/-
3. Medical Expenses Rs. 82,003/-
Saraswathi

R vs B.M.T.C on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188720955/
5
The petitioner is thus entitled to Rs.2,32,003/- which is rounded-off to 2,32,000/- as compensation.

Thus, the petitioner is awarded the total compensation of 2,32,000/-
with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
24.

Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-8934.
There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent is the owner cum insurer of the offending BMTC bus in question.
There is no dispute of the fact that the policy in respect of said vehicle was valid and effective as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".

25. Issue No.3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.2,32,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay the  compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After deposit, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
